hypothesis: Component degradation produces repeatable interpretable signatures in stable cycles
change: No process change; analyze public experimental data using matched factorial comparisons and time-localized features
baseline: Whole-cycle feature pass retained as prior method
measurement: Discovery/verification matched standardized effect; direction consistency; specificity
acceptance_criteria: Discovery |effect|>=1.00 SD and consistency>=90%; verification |effect|>=0.80 SD and consistency>=85%; matching direction
result: Cooler and valve have verified specific signatures; broad pump and accumulator evidence is repeatable but cross-sensitive
decision: Advance a staged proposal; retain ambiguity rather than claim four clean isolations

hypothesis: A development-selected physical-sensor rule can discriminate pump leakage across unseen nuisance-condition combinations inside the source experiment
change: Hold out complete cooler/valve/accumulator condition groups; select feature and threshold on development groups only
measurement: FS1 end-shift threshold; held-out healthy false alarm and weak/severe leak detection
acceptance_criteria: Frozen feature/threshold evaluated only after selection on 9 held-out nuisance groups
result: 0/90 healthy flagged; 90/90 weak leak flagged; 90/90 severe leak flagged
decision: Support the narrow within-experiment pump-screening hypothesis; do not call this external or field validation
